title: Lion Nebula (NIRCam + MIRI image)
caption: The Lion Nebula, NGC 2392, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI. Image Processing: A. Pagan (STScI).

recognition.text: Ranked #15 on ESA/Webb’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: A round nebula shaped like a lion's head floats against black space. At its center a small pinkish-white star forms the lion's button nose, surrounded by purple-pink bubbles and rings that make up the face, while a thick purple-blue ring spreads around it like a mane. This is the planetary nebula NGC 2392, nicknamed the Lion Nebula.

The central star is a white dwarf, the exposed core of a dying star. It is so hot that its radiation is cooking the nebula from the inside, inflating a bubble of ionized hydrogen gas. Tendrils in that bubble are expanding and destroying dust as they go.

Some dust survives. The mane is the inside of a dust shell lit by the core, and compact clumps in it, shown in red and orange, are shielding material behind them. Yellow marks further clumps of molecular hydrogen.

understand.summary: This near- and mid-infrared composite combines Webb's NIRCam and MIRI. The shortest filter is shown in blue, hydrogen light in cyan, molecular hydrogen in yellow, carbon-rich PAH molecules in orange and silicate dust at 10 microns in red.
understand.eye: All of this light is infrared and invisible to the eye, so the colors are assigned to wavelengths we cannot see.

explore: The nebula is a snapshot in time. Shaping the gas and dust like this has taken several thousand years, and the scene keeps changing as the star pushes material away. Astronomers estimate NGC 2392 will disperse in about 10,000 years, a short span in astronomical terms.
Distant galaxies, some with visible spiral arms, dot the background.
alt: A round nebula shaped like a lion's head, with a pinkish-white star at the center, purple-pink bubbles forming a face, and a thick purple-blue ring like a mane, against black space with distant galaxies.
